newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU's Brittan upbeat on early WTO info-tech deal.
newsitem.headline: EU's Brittan upbeat on early WTO info-tech deal.

text.p: European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Tuesday he was hopeful of an early agreement on global trade in information technology products even though negotiations were behind schedule.

"I am hopeful that the good work by...APEC will enable both the U.S. and the key Asian participants to join us in an early broad agreement to reduce trade barrier and business costs worldwide in this vital sector," Brittan said in an address to the Dutch Wholesalers' Association.

Brittan said next month's Singapore conference of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) should seek to clinch an Information Technology Agreement (ITA) to cut tariffs on a wide range of computer products.
His comments echoed an agreement by members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum on Monday to call for the ITA to be concluded at the Singapore conference.
The Singapore conference should also seek to boost technical assistance and increase market access for the least developed countries, Brittan said.
"Neither (of these) alone can solve the problems of the least developed. But more of each is needed as part of a broader solution," he said.
Europe would offer greater market access for a wide range of products from January 1 next year and planned to do more, he said.
In the area of telecommunications, WTO participants needed to boost their offers of increasing market access, Brittan said.

"The significant offer tabled recently in Geneva shows that Europe is prepared to give a lead," he said. "Now we must ensure that Asian partners match that lead. The same goes for America, North and South."
